signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Policy Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags a dominant bilateral theme with USD outperforming (+0.584% 1W avg across 9 pairs) and SEK lagging (−0.727% 1W avg across 2 pairs), creating a 1.311% spread. USD/SEK trades at 9.689, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 9.552), while the Economic Surprise Index underscores fundamental divergence with USD at +1.7 against SEK at a severe −22.6. Sweden's latest CPI print missed expectations at −0.3% m/m versus 0.2% forecast, reinforcing SEK weakness, while Fed 3.75% vs SEK 1.75% provides a +200bp carry advantage for the dollar. Trade bias: Long USD/SEK; broad dollar strength and Swedish disinflation drive trend continuation. Catalyst: US Retail Sales release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Scorecard spread compresses below 0.80%, signaling an abatement of the G10 bilateral divergence.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Differential + Options Put Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 154.82, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 157.62). BoJ holds at 1.0%. Speculative positioning shows JPY COT Leveraged Funds net short at −53,255, though a massive WoW add of +58,042 reflects rapid short covering. The 25d Risk Reversals print at −1.95, indicating a strong options put skew as institutional players buy downside protection against intervention or BoJ hawkishness. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry advantage dominates while spot holds below intervention-alert zones. Catalyst: BoJ Rate Decision on 18 Sep. Risk: A hawkish BoJ hike combined with VIX breaking above 25 forces an abrupt carry unwind.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rate Differential + Positioning Squeeze
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1539, maintaining a position above its SMA50 at 1.1532 but below the SMA20/200 level at 1.1630. Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.65% establishes a 110bp rate differential favoring USD (+143bp on an OIS SOFR/€STR basis), keeping structural topside capped. COT Leveraged Funds remain net short EUR at −46,381 contracts (34th percentile), though WoW flows show +6,403 adds as specs cover shorts ahead of upcoming central bank decisions. One-month ATM implied volatility sits at 5.1% against 4.4% 30-day realized volatility, yielding a modest +0.7% vol risk premium. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; monetary policy divergence limits upside recovery. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech at 15:15 UTC today. Risk: A decisive close above the 1.1630 SMA cluster triggers a broader spec short-squeeze.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT Extreme vs OIS Carry Advantage
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7116, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 0.7168). COT Leveraged Funds show AUD net long at +48,379 contracts, placing positioning at the 93rd percentile (z-score +1.72) of its 52-week range—a crowded speculative long setup. Conversely, retail sentiment sits at 73% short, presenting a sharp institutional versus retail divergence. AONIA at 4.35% vs SOFR at 3.62% yields a −73bp OIS carry differential favoring the Australian dollar, reinforced by RBA rate hike expectations. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; carry advantage supports the pair despite late-trend positioning saturation. Catalyst: US Retail Sales release at 12:30 UTC. Risk: A sharp risk-off shift flattens carry demand and triggers an unwind of crowded spec longs.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Volatility Complacency + Carry Support
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8178, operating above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 0.8074). Fed 3.75% vs SNB 0.00% creates a +375bp carry differential favoring the dollar, providing steady structural support. Options markets exhibit notable complacency, with 1M implied volatility at 6.8% versus 30-day realized volatility at 7.5%, generating a negative vol risk premium of −0.7%. The 25d Risk Reversals print at −0.43, reflecting only a mild put skew despite the Swiss Franc's positive Economic Surprise Index (+22.8). Trade bias: Bullish USD/CHF; substantial carry buffer offsets mild option-market mispricing. Catalyst: SNB Interest Rate Decision on 24 Sep. Risk: A sudden surge in global market volatility triggers flight-to-safety flows into CHF.
